senses.gloss: m. (v. סְרָק) [desert-dweller,] pr. n. Sarḳí (Saracenus), a nomadic trading tribe (v. Sm. Dict. Rom. a. Greek Geogr. s. v. Saraceni).
units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 48:9">Gen. R. s. 48</cite> <he>אחד נדמה לו בדמות ס׳ וכ׳</he> Ar. (ed. <he>סרקי</he>, corr. acc.) one of the angels appeared to him as a Sarḳí, one asa Nabatæan &c.; Yalk. ib. 82 <cite ref="O00860"><he>סִירְקִי</he></cite>.—Pl. <cite ref="O01677"><he>סַרְקִין</he></cite>, <he>סַרְקִיִּין</he>. Y’lamd. to Num. XXIV, 6; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 771:7">Yalk. Num. 771</cite> (ref. to <he>אֲהָלִים</he>, Num. l. c.) <he>בקש לעשותן כאֹהָלִים של ס׳ וכ׳</he> he (Balaam) wanted to make them like the tents of the Saracens which are removed from place to place.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Yoma 6:3:5">Y. Yoma VI, 43ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>הס׳ אוכלין אותו</he> the desert dwellers ate it (the scape-goat that escaped death).
